chunk_map.heading: A file it reads every time

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: line 4: "So far the context has been one message you typed." Closest to violating: "the context" is a definite noun not defined in this file, but it is the arc-earned spine term (host lecture context-is-king.md places this slide after "The first piece of the picture", include line 14). Harm (unresolvable referent) absent: "That's a guardrail" at line 8 resolves to the file of line 6.

line 4: "So far the context has been..." Closest to violating; "So far" is an immediate-continuation opener inside the host deck, not a pointer at another file by title or position. No "the opening lecture"-type callback anywhere (9-line body).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no "the X you did/saw/caught" backward reference to a beat

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no live-demo guess/reveal beat; no terminal-aimed cue or screen-only pronoun (muted read of lines 4-8 has verbed sentences)

rules_evaluated.evidence: line 6: "What if the context was a file the agent reads at the start of every conversation?" carries a self-standing claim (context as a persistent file). Not a wait-state slide.

header line 1 "A file it reads every time" vs body line 6: "a file the agent reads at the start of every conversation". Header "it" resolves to "the agent" in the same chunk; header is literally true of the content.

line 4 "Ephemeral. Gone when you close the chat window." and line 6 "Same mechanism. Different shelf life." are fragment pairs, not a "Not X. Not Y. Z." frame; line 8 "That's a guardrail. That's your turn." is an anaphora pair, not a triple. No superlative, no number, no abstraction stack, no verb triplet. Closest: line 8 pair, which stays inside the pair allowance.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest: "shelf life" (line 6), "guardrail" (line 8): ordinary engineering words, not repo dialect; grep for surface-noun/firing/compendium/forcing function/beat/mood → none in 9-line body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep "\*\*" → 0 bold in body; budget is <=1.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: slide file included by host decks (context-is-king.md line 14, claude-basics personal-site-with-guardrails); presence is a host-file property, and a standalone slide has no phase wrapper to test

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no Phase/Step numbered headers or hand-numbered position

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -ciE "below|above|further down|see below" → 0; node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js | grep -c a-file-it-reads → 0 matches.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/slides/a-file-it-reads-every-time.md → "every slide is within limits"; wc -w → 69, 0 bullets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: header "A file it reads every time" is a noun-phrase lecture heading, not an imperative; this is a lecture-slide where the heading names the subject of the beat (catalogue/orientation, "not every header owes a claim"). Closest to violating: the slide does teach a claim (lines 6-8) that the header only labels; stays inside by the orientation/catalogue exemption.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest: line 8 "That's a guardrail. That's your turn." could be an aphorism kicker (16c), but it adds the term (guardrail) and the hand-off to the exercise, neither restated elsewhere on the slide, so it earns its slot. Line 4 "Ephemeral." is a one-word contrast the slide uses.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no maintainer provenance note of a rename; single-chunk slide whose body matches its header

notes: No maintainer or backing block in the slide file; no accept-notes. Judged sequentially against host decks (context-is-king.md, claude-basics personal-site-with-guardrails). Line 8 'That's your turn' presumes an exercise hand-off; fit depends on host placement, not a defect in this file.
